newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's ultimate EMU goal always been to add jobs.
newsitem.headline: Spain's ultimate EMU goal always been to add jobs.

text.p: Spain's conservative government said on Tuesday the fight against unemployment has always been the ultimate goal of its plan to join Europe's single currency.
"For us the introduction of employment (targets) is not new," said Spanish Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro.
"(And) it doesn't raise any problem given that the entire government economic plan is drawn up to boost employment," he added.
EU partners including Britain and France have both prposed job creation schemes in recent days, with measures such as giving aid to small and medium firms to provide more jobs.
France, in particular, has spoken out for a more social Europe and requested time to think over a stability plan that would impose tough fiscal discipline after EMU starts.

But Spain, which has already committed itself to the Stability Pact, said its convergence plan "isn't causing any difficulties for society... It favours steady, stable growth with job creation," Montoro said.
Montoro stressed that despite the Franch request for time before final approval of the Stability Pact, no-one was questioning a timely European economic and Monetary Union.
Earlier he said also that a delay of EMU was politically impossible.
And he suggested that the achievement of a solid economic base was the best way to fight unemployment.

"An approach in favour of employment all around Europe ultimately means an approach in favour of more economic rationality, cutting (budget) deficits, inflation and ( pursuing) a healthy balance of payments," Montoro said.
